title: Logical Volume Management
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Logical Volume Management and identify key concepts from the supplied syllabus.
Use an appropriate read-only check or controlled example to demonstrate logical volume management.
Describe one common failure mode, safety consideration, or platform/version difference relevant to this topic.

content.intro: This lesson introduces logical volume management as part of disks, filesystems, and storage management. Begin with an observation you can safely repeat, then explain what the result tells you and what it does not prove.
content.why_it_matters: Inspect storage safely and understand filesystems, mounts, logical volumes, RAID, encryption, and recovery constraints.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First, state what you expect from the example. Run it in the intended environment, capture standard output and any error message, and inspect the exit status where meaningful. Then connect the observation to this lesson: Logical Volume Management. Do not infer more than the evidence supports.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake
content_blocks.text: A common mistake is to assume logical volume management behaves identically on every distribution, kernel, utility version, and administrative policy. Verify the installed tool and consult the matching manual before using the procedure elsewhere.

content_blocks.title: Safety and compatibility
content_blocks.text: This is an inspection command. Formatting, partitioning, and repair commands can destroy data. For commands that edit files, manage services, change network/firewall state, partition disks, change permissions recursively, or alter boot settings, use an isolated VM, take a snapshot/backup, review the exact target, and prepare a recovery path before acting.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the command is missing, check whether the required package is installed and which distribution you are using. If access is denied, do not immediately escalate to root; confirm the target path, identity, and required permission. If the result differs, capture the command, output, version, and environment so the issue can be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember the core relationship: Storage changes can destroy data. Identify the intended device, understand the filesystem and mount layers, and test configuration in a VM. The goal is to explain the observed result, test a boundary case, and record a limitation rather than memorize a command in isolation.

content.task: In an isolated Linux lab, investigate logical volume management. Use the guided example as a starting point, record the output/status, and test one boundary, failure, or distribution-specific case. Explain what you learned without changing a production system.
